name: Congenitally Uncorrected Transposition of the Great Arteries with Coarctation
aliases: Congenital Transposition of the Great Arteries and Coarctation of the Aorta

criteria.description: Presence of ventriculoarterial discordance with the aorta arising from the morphological right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the morphological left ventricle
Narrowing or constriction of the aortic isthmus or descending aorta consistent with coarctation
Echocardiographic evidence demonstrating both transposition and coarctation features
Signs of congestive heart failure or differential blood pressure between upper and lower limbs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anatomical ventriculoarterial discordance with coarctation confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis typically requires multimodal imaging including echocardiography and cardiac MRI or angiography.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cyanosis due to systemic venous blood entering systemic circulation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Differential blood pressure and pulses between upper and lower extremities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to coarctation of the aorta

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating ventriculoarterial discordance and coarctation
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming anatomical details
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy or conduction abnormalities
Pulse oximetry revealing differential oxygen saturation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance with physiologically corrected circulation
Usually absence of cyanosis in early life
Absence of transposition features on imaging
Presentation primarily with hypertension and murmur

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Marked blood pressure discrepancy between limbs
